title: GC Pressure Causes RenderingServer Allocated RID to disappear
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot 4.6

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9174) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

RenderingServer instances created via InstanceCreate2 disappear when C# GC pressure is high, even though their RIDs remain valid.

When instances are created using RenderingServer.InstanceCreate2 in C#, they can visually disappear from the scene after enough GC pressure accumulates. The instances' RIDs continue to report IsValid = true, the scenario RID does not change, and no error is logged. The rendering simply stops displaying the instances.

The issue scales with GC pressure — allocating 1MB per frame causes disappearance within seconds, while lower allocation rates delay it proportionally => 128 bytes per frame at 240fps took us approximately 440 seconds. With zero allocations the instances remain visible indefinitely

We really appreciate the performance we have been able to achieve when using RenderingServer RIDs, so a fix for this would be very important for us - even a reinitialization handler for whenever RIDs are dropped and need to be reinitialized would be great.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the attached minimal project in Godot 4.6
Run the scene
Enable the "GC Stress" toggle in the top-left corner
Observe the red box disappearing within a few seconds
Note that the label continues to show instance=True and world=True even after the box is gone
